bullets.title: NVDA: CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid Chinese spy scandal; multiple downgrades, PT cuts
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA President/CEO after the board opened an independent investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset who facilitated $7.5B+ in chip shipments to China; Colette Kress named interim CEO. The week saw 7+ sell-side downgrades (Melius to Hold $185 from $315; Evercore to In-Line $186 from $465; Oppenheimer to Perform; KeyBanc to Sector Weight; Bernstein to Market Perform $200; Baird to Neutral $200; Craig-Hallum to Hold $189; HSBC to Hold $170). Consensus shifted to 10x CY27 EPS as trough floor (~$150-170), with retail buying $1.6B on Thursday and GS cutting to $220 on key-man/China risk; Evercore's Semis bear case pegs FY2 P/E compressing to 8x, implying material downside from prior highs. DOJ pursuing antitrust and multiple China-linked probes; MATCH Act and AI OVERWATCH Act gaining Congressional traction.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings preview (Nov 17): beat expected but 2028 visibility is the key debate
bullets.body: Consensus expects Oct-Q revenue ~$109B (vs $108B guide) with EPS ~$2.49-2.52; Jan-Q seen at $125B on Rubin ramp. Gross margin guidance is the swing factor—Citi models 71.5% vs Street 72.1% on HBM price increases and early Rubin costs. Investor focus has shifted entirely to 2028 order visibility, neocloud backlog conversion, and whether interim CEO Kress will honor Huang's $164B+ ecosystem financing commitments including the $250B OpenAI backstop she had reportedly opposed.

bullets.title: CSCO: Big beat and raise on AI hyperscaler ramp; FY27 AI revenue target raised to $9B
bullets.body: Cisco Q1 FY27 revenue $18.52B beat FactSet $18.12B; EPS $1.40 beat $1.33. FY27 guidance raised to $74.8-75.8B with AI hyperscaler revenue target increased from $7.5B to $9B (+125% YoY), representing 12% of total revenue. Product orders +21% YoY; firewall orders grew 30%+ for a third consecutive quarter. Morgan Stanley maintains Equal-Weight at $120 PT citing gross margin headwinds from hyperscaler mix in FY28; KeyBanc raises to OW at $135 PT. Stock faded on order deceleration to 21% from 35% last quarter and GM compression.

bullets.title: FOXA: Morgan Stanley names Top Pick at $90 PT (37% upside) after Roku deal closes early
bullets.body: Fox closed its $22B Roku acquisition earlier than the initial 1H27 expected timeline. MS resumes Overweight and elevates to Top Pick: pro forma revenue growth lifts to ~6% (from low-single-digits) and EBITDA CAGR rises from ~1% to ~9% (CY27-30E); FCF/share compounds at ~20% through FY30. $400M+ cost synergies modeled; Fox+Tubi+Roku Channel combined hold 10%+ monthly US TV viewership, rivaling Disney and ahead of Netflix. Net leverage falls from 2.8x to ~1x by FY29. Bull/bear skew 4:1 ($100/$60).

bullets.title: NBIS: Q3 massive beat; 2027 revenue guided $12-13B (4x growth) but FY26 lowered on site delays
bullets.body: Nebius Q3 revenue $980.8M beat FactSet $907.2M; adj. EBITDA $465.8M crushed $351.8M consensus; ARR $6.4B vs $4.70B expected. GPU pricing up >20% QoQ; ACV/MW exceeded $25M vs $20M in Q2. Customer prepayments now cover >100% of associated capex (up from 50-60% in Q2). FY26 revenue guided to low end of $3.0-3.4B on Vineland NJ power transition delays; FY27 guided $12-13B with $40-45B capex; pre-tax breakeven by end of 2027. Citi raises to Buy, $265 PT; Morgan Stanley Equal-Weight at $144 citing deployment risk.

bullets.title: CRWV: Q3 beat and raise; sold out through 2027; $9B prepayments reduce financing risk
bullets.body: CoreWeave Q3 revenue $3.66B (+168% YoY) beat Street $3.56B; non-GAAP operating margins 10.4% well above 6.9% expected. FY26 guidance raised with operating income midpoint +26%; exit ARR raised to $20-21B. GPU pricing +25% in July and +10% in Q3; short-duration contracts >$40M/MW, 4-5yr at $20-25M/MW. Management expects <$5B parent-level equity raises through 2027; no unsecured debt needed. Citi raises PT to $149; JPM reiterates OW at $125; UBS Buy at $105. Stock had fallen 40%+ prior to print on credit concerns.

bullets.title: HUBS: Co-founder Halligan returns as CEO in 'refounding'; CFO from Adobe joins
bullets.body: Yamini Rangan stepped down immediately; co-founder Brian Halligan returned as CEO on Nov 12. CFO Kate Bueker retiring Feb 11, 2027; Adobe's Karen Burgess joins as EVP Finance Nov 30 and becomes CFO Feb 11. Company reaffirmed Q4/FY26 guidance. JPM views as positive catalyst to address expansion slowdown and AI monetization path. Wolfe maintains Peer Perform with FY27/28 growth modeled at 10%/8% vs consensus 11%/11%; fair value range $150-260.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi downgrades to Neutral; GTA VI launch (11/19) and fading Steal An Egg pose 4Q risk
bullets.body: Citi downgrades Roblox from Buy to Neutral citing Steal An Egg CCU down ~56% from September peak, no breakout hit emerging in top 10, and GTA VI launching Nov 19. Month-to-date November CCUs down 21%, implying 4Q26 bookings of ~$1.92B, slightly below guidance midpoint of $1.95B. PT maintained at $55 (28x 2028 FCF). Management noted limited data to size GTA VI competitive impact.

bullets.title: TLN: Oppenheimer initiates Outperform at $400 PT; 750 MW long-term capacity deal locks cash flows
bullets.body: TLN signed a 750 MW long-term capacity agreement for PJM delivery years 2029/2030-2035/2036 generating ~$100M/year. Oppenheimer initiates Outperform at $400 PT; base adjusted FCF/share guidance ~$38/$48/$46-50 for 2027/2028/2029E (~30% CAGR). Goldman raised PT to $502. Upside levers include new data center PPAs, faster AWS ramp, and accretive M&A.

bullets.title: AMAT: Q4 beat and raise; 2027 WFE growth guided >30%; multiple banks cut PT on peer de-rating
bullets.body: Applied Materials Q4 EPS $4.16 beat $4.06; revenue $10.41B beat. Q1 guidance: revenue $11.1B and EPS $4.35, both above consensus. Management expects 2027 WFE to grow >30%, AMAT to outperform market. Advanced Packaging +90% YoY; 20+ fab ramps in CY27. Citi raises FY27E EPS ~4% but cuts PT to $580 from $700 on sector multiple compression. GS PT cut to $580 from $670; Wells Fargo PT cut to $500 from $610; B. Riley raises to $500.

bullets.title: DIS: Q4 earnings preview (Nov 17): SVOD margins at 10%, ESPN at 10-year high
bullets.body: Disney reports Q4 before the open Nov 17; consensus $25.16B revenue, $1.68 EPS. Bull case: SVOD margins crossing 10%, record Experiences results, ESPN viewership at 10-year high. Bear case: structural sports-rights cost pressure and secular linear TV declines. FY27 guidance expected to call for double-digit adjusted EPS growth. Options imply ~6.2% post-earnings move; stock up 20.4% since Aug 4.

bullets.title: CHTR: +14% on week from $1.5B debt tender offer; analysts see $27/share equity accretion potential
bullets.body: Charter announced a $1.5B cash tender for bonds trading at ~85% of par, seen as shareholder-accretive. Citi calculates potential $27/sh equity value capture through YE27 via debt discount. Street split on the name: TD Cowen rates Buy at $345, Wells Fargo Underweight at $103, Goldman Sell at $110. Week's gain also aided by telecom sector rotation. EBITDA headwinds from broadband subscriber losses and aggressive go-to-market costs remain ongoing concerns.

bullets.title: INTU: JPM Neutral; valuation cheap at 10x uFCF but share recovery unsustainable without customer acquisition improvement
bullets.body: JPM models F1Q27 revenue $4.297B (+11% YoY), slightly below guidance midpoint; management strategy sacrifices near-term ARPC to drive customer acquisition via entry-level products. Net new customer adds across QuickBooks and TurboTax DIY remain weak. F1Q is first without GoCo acquisition revenue tailwind. JPM forecasts PF EPS $2.50 for F1Q27; reaffirmed FY27 guidance. Citi cuts PT 10% to $285 on CEO investigation risks and lower peer multiples.

bullets.title: IONQ: Gains Commvault CFO Gary Merrill as new CFO; quantum sector broadly weak
bullets.body: IonQ named Commvault's Gary Merrill as new CFO effective early December; Inder Singh stepped down immediately. KeyBanc flagged CVLT's CFO departure negatively given Merrill's influence on GTM organization after ~2 years as Chief Commercial Officer. CVLT reaffirmed F3Q and FY27 guidance; $200 PT maintained at 24.7x CY28E EV/FCF.

bullets.title: AAPL: Reached 52-week high at $360 (+31.6% YTD); upgraded to Buy at China Renaissance ($425 PT)
bullets.body: Apple hit a 52-week high at $360 on Nov 12, +31.6% YTD; China Renaissance upgraded to Buy from Hold with $425 PT (22% upside vs FactSet consensus $341). iPhone Duo return rates above 30% cited as a negative channel check. Apple's on-device AI lagging behind emerging personal assistants per UBS checks. UBS/MS flagged AAPL outperforming Mag7 by 11% MTD despite weak near-term fundamentals.

bullets.title: AMD/AVGO: Biggest beneficiaries of NVDA leadership turmoil; both up ~18-19% on the week
bullets.body: AMD +18.9% and AVGO +18% week-over-week cited as key beneficiaries of NVDA CEO uncertainty; AMD upgraded to Outperform by William Blair and Oppenheimer. AMD's DCAI demand is running ahead of supply through 1H28; CPU revenue expected to double in 2027. AVGO completing significant financing round to support Anthropic's CY27 GPU purchases; has $300M in prepayments. Wolfe names AVGO as best risk/reward among AI compute names with 37.2% upside to $500 PT.

bullets.title: SNDK: 8-for-1 stock split confirmed, ex-date Nov 20
bullets.body: SanDisk executing an 8-for-1 stock split with ex-date November 20, 2026; record date November 9; payable date November 19; fractions paid in cash. No other material company developments in the period.

bullets.title: NET: DZ Bank upgrades to Buy at $300; zero-trust/agentic platform gains
bullets.body: DZ Bank upgraded Cloudflare to Buy from Sell, raising PT to $300 from $275. Cloudflare Q3 revenue $782.5M beat 6.2%; billings beat 7.8%; Q4 guided $845-846M above consensus. Workers platform and Act IV agent monetization generating revenue with broader upside. Wolfe remains Long and Strong in Agentic Infra basket (TWLO, DDOG, SNOW, NET). Cybersecurity stocks broadly bid post-MSFT outage.

bullets.title: MSFT: Widespread O365 outage (not cybersecurity); Ignite conference upcoming; $650 PT from Jefferies
bullets.body: Microsoft suffered a ~16-hour Outlook/Teams/SharePoint outage caused by server CPU usage spike from a rollout—confirmed not a cyberattack. Recovery progressed regionally. Ignite Conference (Nov 17-20) expected to feature Agentic product announcements and AI messaging across Copilot, Azure Foundry, and security. Jefferies maintains Buy at $650 PT. Cybersecurity peers (CRWD, NET, PANW) rallied in sympathy on perceived demand tailwinds.

bullets.title: FSLR: Worst S&P performer week ending Nov 13, down 10.6%; -34.4% YTD
bullets.body: First Solar was the largest S&P 500 weekly decliner at -10.6% for the week ending November 13, now down 34.4% year-to-date. No single new catalyst identified in the period; broader renewable energy sector weakness tied to AI data center policy uncertainty and rising rates. Solar sub-sector broadly weak in power & utilities segment.
